title: What Told the Stomach to Start

scenes.tts: A dog eats a meal. The food falls out of an opening in its neck before it reaches the stomach. Yet the stomach pours out acid juice. What told the stomach to start? The answer came from Pavlov's laboratory in Saint Petersburg.
scenes.visual: A gap opens in the esophagus bar, food drops out, green acid juice appears in the stomach block, a question mark box with a dashed arrow points at the stomach.
scenes.narration: A dog eats a meal. The food falls out of an opening in its neck before it reaches the stomach. Yet the stomach pours out acid juice. What told the stomach to start? The answer came from Pavlov's laboratory in Saint Petersburg.

scenes.tts: Pavlov's laboratory opened the dog's esophagus at the neck, so swallowed food fell out. A gastric fistula let juice drain from the stomach. If juice flowed only when food touched the stomach, the dog should make none. Instead, after a delay of some minutes, abundant acid juice flowed.
scenes.visual: The esophagus splits at the neck, food falls out, a fistula and flask appear, an expected-none note is crossed out, and green juice fills the flask.
scenes.narration: Pavlov's laboratory opened the dog's esophagus at the neck, so swallowed food fell out. A gastric fistula let juice drain from the stomach. If juice flowed only when food touched the stomach, the dog should make none. Instead, after a delay of some minutes, abundant acid juice flowed.

scenes.tts: Then both vagus nerves were cut. The vagus nerves connect the brainstem to the gut. Now eating no longer brought the juice. So in the dog, a nerve-driven cephalic phase exists, carried by the vagus. Sight, smell, taste and chewing of food trigger it. It does not rule out later phases, which run once food is in the stomach or intestine.
scenes.visual: Brainstem and two vagus lines reach the stomach, both are crossed out and the flask empties; sight, smell, taste and chewing chips feed the brainstem; food enters the stomach with a later-phases note.
scenes.narration: Then both vagus nerves were cut. The vagus nerves connect the brainstem to the gut. Now eating no longer brought the juice. So in the dog, a nerve-driven cephalic phase exists, carried by the vagus. Sight, smell, taste and chewing of food trigger it. It does not rule out later phases, which run once food is in the stomach or intestine.

scenes.tts: Later phases are partly chemical. A hormone is a substance released into the blood that acts on distant target cells. Gastrin is one. G cells in the stomach lining release gastrin when food, especially protein, is in the stomach. Gastrin makes the stomach secrete more acid.

scenes.visual: Stomach block with a blood bar; food enters, G cells release yellow gastrin dots into the blood bar, they return to the stomach and green acid increases.
scenes.narration: Later phases are partly chemical. A hormone is a substance released into the blood that acts on distant target cells. Gastrin is one. G cells in the stomach lining release gastrin when food, especially protein, is in the stomach. Gastrin makes the stomach secrete more acid.

scenes.tts: Acid chyme then enters the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine. Its lining releases secretin. Secretin makes pancreatic duct cells secrete a bicarbonate-rich fluid, which neutralizes the stomach's acid. Fats and proteins in the duodenum bring out C C K. C C K drives the pancreas to release enzymes, and the gallbladder to contract and release bile.

CCK drives the pancreas to release enzymes, and the gallbladder to contract and release bile.
scenes.visual: Acid moves from stomach to duodenum; secretin dots travel by a blood bar to the pancreas which sends bicarbonate and the acid fades; CCK dots go to pancreas and gallbladder, enzymes and bile flow into the duodenum.
scenes.narration: Acid chyme then enters the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine. Its lining releases secretin. Secretin makes pancreatic duct cells secrete a bicarbonate-rich fluid, which neutralizes the stomach's acid. Fats and proteins in the duodenum bring out CCK. CCK drives the pancreas to release enzymes, and the gallbladder to contract and release bile.

scenes.tts: Nerves and hormones overlap. Healthy human volunteers were given C C K eight at one dose. Atropine blocks the acetylcholine receptors that nerves use on many glands. With atropine, the pancreatic trypsin response fell by eighty four percent. So at that dose, much of the hormone's effect depended on acetylcholine, and tests on rat pancreas suggested it came from nerves. Block one route, and the fraction that disappears shows how much depends on that route, under those conditions.

With atropine, the pancreatic trypsin response fell by 84%. So at that dose, much of the hormone's effect depended on acetylcholine, and tests on rat pancreas suggested it came from nerves.
